messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks. I don’t want to subsidize A’s purchase; I want my fair share. I’m not saying I want to keep the house, and I haven’t agreed on a sale price or terms. I don’t know how the will divides the house, and the shares and legal details haven’t been settled.

I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, but C hasn’t agreed, and I can’t proceed without her agreement. I don’t have a price to propose yet. I’m not sure what the will says about the house. I know B wants money, but I don’t know what for.

I can understand C’s concern; I don’t think a “family discount” should be assumed. I’m not sure what the house should sell for or how the shares should work, and I know C hasn’t agreed to A buying it. I would like some money from the estate to start a dance studio. I haven’t settled on an amount.
Yes. Let’s review the will and estate documents and get an independent appraisal. That doesn’t commit me to any sale terms.
Yes, finding out what the will says and getting a professional appraisal sound like sensible first steps. I still hope we can discuss a family discount, but no price is decided.
Yes, that sounds sensible. It would help to know what the will provides and what funds might be available before I can say what I could use for the studio.
I don’t know who the executor is or where the will is held. Let’s find out.
I don’t know who the executor is or where the will is held.
I’m not sure who the executor is or where the will is being kept. We’ll need to check.
I can check his papers for a lawyer’s details. If I find them, I’ll contact the lawyer and report back.
I can check whether Dad had a lawyer and contact them if I can find out who it was. I’ll report back.
I can check his papers to see whether he had a lawyer, and contact them if I find one.
I’ll check his papers at home for the lawyer’s details and report back if I find them.
I don’t know who Dad’s lawyer was, so I can’t contact the office yet. C is checking his papers for the details.
I’ll check the bank or other records for any details of his lawyer and report back.
